transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-11-06 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Recording: cloud.fireflies... (link omitted)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Lee, AE at Redwood, and with me is Priya Nair, our principal SE. Evan may pop in later. Marcus, Samir, great to meet you all.
[00:12] Marcus Hale: Hey Jordan, hi Priya. Thanks for fitting us in. We've been evaluating partners to help us onboard GPU-backed inference into our channel partners.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Thanks Marcus. Quick agenda from our side: run through Velociti's use cases and topology, talk about how Redwood can integrate with your partners (reseller/managed service pattern), and surface any security or procurement constraints.
[00:38] Lena Ortiz: Quick note — we're primarily focused on two things: low-latency small-seq webhooks (avg 64 tokens) for inference and a secondary batch embed pipeline. Also need per-tenant isolation because resellers want separate billing.
[00:52] Jordan Lee: Got it. Per-tenant billing and isolation, plus latency on small sequences. That's a common pattern. Can you give us a sense of expected QPS/p95 targets?
[01:05] Marcus Hale: Right now proof-of-concept is 200 concurrent requests across five partners, p95 target 180ms end-to-end. Ideally want sub-200ms for our web UI. Cost sensitivity is high — partners expect reasonable margins.
[01:25] Priya Nair: Ok, couple quick clarifying q's: Are these partners running in their own VPCs or will Velociti provide a central proxy? And any data residency constraints?
[01:35] Samir Gupta: Most partners will be in their own VPCs but we also have a couple that prefer a managed option where we run the inference and resell. No strict country-level residency yet but some partners in EU request data residency.
[01:48] Jordan Lee: That maps to two integration patterns we see: 1) Channel-managed hosted model — Redwood hosted API with routing & multi-tenant isolation, and 2) Private deployment for reseller (VPC or on-prem) where Redwood ships a private control plane. Both can support per-tenant billing.
[02:05] Marcus Hale: Can you explain more about the private deployment? Our security team will ask about KMS and audit logs.
[02:12] Priya Nair: Sure. In private mode we provide a customer-controlled control plane that can be deployed in a VPC; you retain keys with KMS/HSM integrations, and we integrate with SAML SSO + SCIM for RBAC. Audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM or retained locally. There was a note about some customers calling it "Redwood Privatee" in older notes — apologies for the typo.
[02:34] Renee Park: (Security) We need proof points: SOC2 report, ISO blurb, and detailed encryption-at-rest/in-transit matrix. Also need to verify ability to bring your own KMS and ensure no token leak into hosted logs.
[02:47] Jordan Lee: Understood. I'll send our latest SOC2 and security pack. We support BYOK via standard KMS integrations; logs can be configured so that request bodies are not forwarded.
[02:59] Lena Ortiz: About latency: if we go hosted and route requests through Redwood's hosted API, what kind of tail latency variations do customers see? Some vendors have big p99 jumps under burst.
[03:12] Priya Nair: Good question — two parts. Our serving runtime is tuned for small-seq workloads with continuous batching and KV cache management; for short sequences p95s are typically sub-100ms on dedicated pools in the same region, p99s depend on burst and batch windows. For channel-managed hosted, we can pin partner traffic to dedicated pools to guarantee stability.
[03:35] Marcus Hale: What's the margin math for us as a reseller? If we resell hosted capacity, how are payouts handled?
[03:43] Jordan Lee: There are a few models — wholesale pricing on committed capacity, a pass-through usage model, or a blended reseller margin. We can do reserved capacity with committed discounts which makes unit economics predictable for your partners. We'll share a pricing matrix.
[03:58] Samir Gupta: We have one technical blocker: we use a custom auth header pattern and our integrations team wants to avoid long-lived API keys. We prefer token exchange via our identity layer.
[04:10] Priya Nair: We support token exchange flows and short-lived tokens; can integrate with your identity broker. Also support SSO for console access.
[04:20] Jordan Lee: On the topic of high-concurrency small seq, one practical lever is to enable prefix-KV caching for common prompts across partners, that brings down tokens and latency. Another is quantized model variants for price-sensitive partners.
[04:35] Lena Ortiz: Is quantization something you do automatically or is that manual model selection?
[04:39] Priya Nair: We give recommendations via Redwood Optimize — automated suggestions for quantization and batching by workload. But customers control pinning a model variant for sensitivity reasons.
[04:50] Marcus Hale: Competitors like CloudScale pushed their own edge adapters. How is Redwood different if partners care about control?
[04:59] Jordan Lee: Short answer: runtime + orchestration plus ops tooling. We focus on predictable inference economics and have a unified API across hosted, dedicated, and private. For partners wanting full control we can offer private deployments and a partner-friendly control-plane integration.
[05:12] Lena Ortiz: We want an integration pattern that allows our partners to optionally take over serving later — a migration path.
[05:18] Priya Nair: Totally feasible. We commonly do an initial hosted pilot, then a dedicated reserved pool, and later offer a private drop-in adapter for partners who want to host. We maintain the same API contracts to ease migration.
[05:33] Jordan Lee: For the pilot we'd recommend a scoped workload: 1-2 partners, synthetic traffic and a replay of a day of production with your sample traces. Priya will propose a benchmark plan.
[05:43] Marcus Hale: Sounds good. What about observability and per-route cost breakdowns? Partners will ask for per-tenant token-level billing.
[05:52] Priya Nair: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost + latency breakdown by route/model. You can also pull detailed CSV exports or stream events to your billing system. For reseller cases you can configure customer-specific rate limits and quotas.
[06:05] Renee Park: On compliance we also need to ensure we can run vulnerability scans and have a SOC2 subservice doc.
[06:12] Jordan Lee: We can share the SOC2 and the subservice list. For private deployments you can run scans in your environment; for hosted we provide penetration test summaries and we have timelines for deeper audits under enterprise agreements.
[06:25] Marcus Hale: A couple of tactical things — will Redwood accept our standard MSA terms? We often need modify indemnity and data handling clauses.
[06:33] Jordan Lee: We'll need our legal team to review; pilot NDAs are usually straightforward. For enterprise contracts we have flexibility — the details vary but we've worked with similar channel partners. I'll loop in contracts after this call.
[06:44] Samir Gupta: For the benchmark, our main metrics are p95 latency, p99 tail, token cost per 1k tokens, and throughput for batched embedding jobs. We also want cold-start behavior for larger contexts.
[06:56] Priya Nair: We'll include those metrics. Also curious: what's your traffic distribution (seq length histogram)? That helps us configure batching windows and kernel selection.
[07:06] Lena Ortiz: We'll share a histogram. Average seq 64, median 40, 95th 420. Embedding jobs are larger but intermittent.
[07:16] Jordan Lee: Great. One note on model selection: for small seqs the Llama variants with quantization often hit the best cost/latency tradeoff; for high-quality generation you can choose a larger model but cost goes up.
[07:28] Marcus Hale: Any benchmarks or public numbers we can look at?
[07:31] Priya Nair: I'll share a short benchmark deck and a spreadsheet with example perf numbers — those are region and hardware dependent, but it should give you a starting point.
[07:40] Marcus Hale: Great.
[07:42] (brief cross talk, background noise)
[08:05] Jordan Lee: Recap and proposed immediate next steps: Jordan will share security pack and pricing matrix by Nov 9–10; Marcus to share traffic samples and architecture by Nov 12; Priya to propose benchmark plan and schedule technical deep dive w/SEs during week of Nov 16. Also propose a pilot scope doc for 2 partners for 4 weeks.
[08:30] Lena Ortiz: That timeline works; we'll try to get the samples early.
[08:36] Marcus Hale: One more question — do you have any reference customers in telco or MSP reseller channels?
[08:43] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have two MSP channel partners (names omitted) who've run similar pilots; happy to connect you if useful.
[08:51] Renee Park: Also will expect an architecture review with our security team before any pilot sign-off.
[08:56] Priya Nair: No problem. We'll schedule a security-focused session.
[09:02] Jordan Lee: Anything else?
[09:05] Samir Gupta: Not from me.
[09:07] Marcus Hale: That's it. Thanks everyone.

[58:00] End of recording.
